standard_prerequisites.name: Free systems on finitely many generators
standard_prerequisites.statement: F_n is the free system on n generators, and it embeds into F_m when n is at most m.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two systems compared.

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementarity transfers from the inclusion
standard_prerequisites.statement: If one model is an elementary subsystem of another then the inclusion is an elementary embedding.
standard_prerequisites.use: It turns the failure of an embedding into a contradiction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Surjectivity of elementary self-embeddings
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every elementary embedding of F_n into itself is surjective.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the statement contradicted at the end.

core_obligations: Assume an elementary embedding of F_m into F_n with m larger than n, and take a copy of F_m extending F_n in a way that the inclusion is elementary (source line 1091).

Use that the copy is an elementary extension of F_n to obtain an elementary embedding of F_m into itself whose image is not everything, contradicting the surjectivity of elementary self-embeddings (source line 1093).

proof_roadmap.step: Choose an elementary extension of F_n by a copy of F_m.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 1089-1090: for n at least three and m larger than n there is no elementary embedding of the free system on m generators into the free system on n generators, even though the latter embeds into the former. The proof (source lines 1091-1094) builds the contradiction by taking a copy of the larger free system extending the smaller one so that the inclusion is elementary, which converts the assumed embedding into an elementary embedding of the larger system into itself with a proper image; that is precisely what the preceding surjectivity proposition forbids. The statement records the non-existence and neither the construction of the elementary extension nor the reduction to the self-embedding case.
